name: Methanol-to-olefins (MTO, DMTO)
applications: ethylene and propylene from coal- or gas-derived methanol
polyethylene and polypropylene in coal-rich regions
principle: Methanol vapour is converted over a SAPO-34 molecular sieve catalyst in a fluidized-bed reactor into ethylene and propylene. The catalyst coke is burned off in a regenerator, and the product gas is quenched, compressed and separated. DMTO-II adds a second reactor that cracks C4 and heavier by-products over a dual-function catalyst to raise olefin yield; DMTO-III raises selectivity further without recycling C4+.

process_steps.name: Fluidized-bed reactor
equipment: shallow turbulent fluidized-bed reactor with SAPO-34 catalyst

process_steps.name: Olefin separation
equipment: cold box and fractionation as in a cracker

performance.metric: ethylene plus propylene selectivity, demonstration unit

source.note: Ye, Tian and Liu, DMTO: A Sustainable Methanol-to-Olefins Technology, Engineering 7(1), 2021, pp. 17-21 (figures to end-2019)

performance.metric: methanol consumption per tonne of light olefins, original process
performance.basis: DICP; 2.85 with newer catalyst, about 2.64 for DMTO-III

source.note: Ye, Tian and Liu, DMTO: A Sustainable Methanol-to-Olefins Technology, Engineering 7(1), 2021, pp. 17-21 (figures to end-2019)

performance.basis: 14 started up; licensed olefins capacity 14 Mt/yr, 7.67 Mt/yr in the 14 started units

source.note: Ye, Tian and Liu, DMTO: A Sustainable Methanol-to-Olefins Technology, Engineering 7(1), 2021, pp. 17-21 (figures to end-2019)

reference_plants.name: Shenhua Baotou coal-to-olefins plant
reference_plants.capacity: 1.8 Mt/yr methanol feed, 600,000 t/yr polyethylene and polypropylene (first commercial DMTO)

source.note: Ye, Tian and Liu, DMTO: A Sustainable Methanol-to-Olefins Technology, Engineering 7(1), 2021, pp. 17-21 (figures to end-2019)

advantages: Fluidized-bed process proven at multi-million-tonne scale in China
limitations: Methanol feed from coal brings a high CO2 footprint
Needs about 2.6-3.0 t methanol per tonne of olefins
